correctness.rationale: On each Arnold block, inversion negates the ordered phases. Summation by parts still bounds the inverse itself because the variation of exp(-i theta_j) is at most the telescoping phase variation. For rotated Cesaro multipliers, \(F_m(\phi-\theta_j)\) has exactly the same adjacent-difference magnitudes as \(F_m(-\phi+\theta_j)\), by \(F_m(-t)=\overline{F_m(t)}\); Arnold's geometric-phase variation lemma therefore supplies the same uniform bound. The direct sum is consequently invertible and both \(T\) and \(T^{-1}\) are uniformly Kreiss bounded. Arnold's independent signed-average lower estimate for \(T\) is unchanged and proves non-SCB. No experimental extrapolation is used.
